page: Microsoft Azure M64m is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8280M processor running at 2.7 GHz on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled on the x86_64 architecture. Its defining characteristic is an expansive memory capacity of 1,792 GB RAM, delivering 28 GB of memory per vCPU. Hardware features include 38 MB of L3 cache, support for AVX and AVX-512 extensions, and AES cryptographic instructions. For local storage needs, it integrates 7,697 GB of bundled local SSD storage, while operating without discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark metrics reveal a distinct divergence between single-threaded and parallel processing capabilities. Due to the modest clock frequency and architectural generation, single-core metrics fall into lower percentiles, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 906.0 and stress-ng single-core throughput of 1038.28. In contrast, multi-threaded workloads leverage the wide core count to achieve average tier performance, registering 43,783.83 on stress-ng multi-core and 9,399.0 on Geekbench multi-core. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate solid throughput, reaching 182.37 GB/sec for large block reads and 73.3 GB/sec for writes. In application benchmarks, the instance delivers 39.98 million operations per second on Redis SET tests alongside consistent database transaction throughput.

Given its massive memory footprint paired with bundled high-capacity local SSD storage, the M64m is engineered primarily for large in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, high-throughput caching systems, and heavy transactional database environments. Because the architecture prioritizes capacity and aggregate throughput over per-core clock speed, workloads requiring high single-threaded responsiveness or low-latency large language model token generation will encounter bottlenecks, making this profile best reserved for memory-bound enterprise services.
description: Microsoft Azure M64m is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8280M processor running at 2.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance pairs its compute resources with an extensive 1,792 GB of RAM and 7,697 GB of bundled local SSD storage, without discrete GPU acceleration. Benchmark results show average multi-core processing performance, robust memory read bandwidth of 182.37 GB/sec, and high throughput on in-memory operations like Redis, though single-core compute speeds fall into lower performance tiers. The resource allocation yields a high RAM-to-vCPU ratio of 28 GB per core, offering qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive rather than compute-bound operations. Consequently, the M64m is engineered for massive in-memory databases, large-scale caching platforms, and data-intensive enterprise workloads requiring vast memory space rather than high single-threaded clock frequencies.
